soil: Clay or clay loam that holds water
tips: Use certified, treated seed of a variety suited to your season and region.
Alternate wetting and drying saves water without lowering yield.
Apply nitrogen in 2-3 split doses instead of one heavy dose.

stages.name: Nursery and transplanting
tasks: Prepare a raised, well-drained nursery bed and use treated, healthy seed.
Level the main field and mix in well-decomposed farmyard manure before puddling.
Transplant 20-25 day old seedlings in lines, 2-3 seedlings per hill.

stages.name: Tillering
tasks: Keep 2-3 cm of water in the field; avoid long periods of deep flooding.
Weed by hand or with a weeder around 20-25 days after transplanting.
Apply nitrogen in split doses as per soil test or local recommendation and scout for stem borer.

stages.name: Panicle initiation and flowering
tasks: Do not let the field dry out at flowering; keep shallow water.
Scout for blast, brown planthopper and bacterial leaf blight; avoid excess nitrogen.
Install pheromone traps if stem borer moths are seen.

stages.name: Grain filling and maturity
tasks: Reduce water gradually and drain the field about 10 days before harvest.
Harvest when about 80-85% of the grains turn golden yellow.
Dry grain to about 12-14% moisture before storage.

tips: Sow on time; late sowing reduces yield.
Irrigation at crown root initiation, tillering, flowering and grain filling is most important.
Use treated seed and a variety recommended for your area.

stages.name: Germination and crown root stage
tasks: Sow treated seed in a well-prepared bed.
Give the first irrigation at crown root initiation, about 20-25 days after sowing.
Control early weeds as per recommendation.

stages.name: Tillering
tasks: Top-dress nitrogen as per soil test after the first irrigation.
Irrigate again at about 40-45 days when tillering peaks.
Scout for yellow rust and aphids.

stages.name: Jointing and flowering
tasks: Irrigate at jointing and flowering; these are critical stages.
Look for yellow stripes on leaves (yellow rust) and report early to your agriculture officer.
Avoid spraying in strong wind.

stages.name: Grain filling and maturity
tasks: Irrigate lightly at grain filling if the soil is dry.
Stop irrigation as the crop turns yellow.
Harvest when grains are hard and straw is golden; dry well before storage.

soil: Well-drained loam; maize does not tolerate waterlogging
tips: Good drainage is essential; waterlogging for even a day or two can damage the crop.
Scout the whorl for fall armyworm every 2-3 days in the first 8 weeks.
Water stress at tasseling and silking reduces yield the most.

stages.name: Emergence
tasks: Sow treated seed in rows and keep a healthy plant stand.
Ensure good drainage.
Do the first weeding at 15-20 days.

stages.name: Vegetative growth
tasks: Earth up and top-dress nitrogen as per recommendation at about 25-30 days.
Scout the whorl for fall armyworm (ragged leaves, sawdust-like droppings).
Irrigate if there is no rain for a week.

stages.name: Tasseling and silking
tasks: Do not allow water stress; this is the most critical stage.
Keep the field weed-free.
Continue scouting for armyworm and stem borer.

stages.name: Grain filling and maturity
tasks: Maintain light irrigation until the dough stage.
Harvest when husks dry and kernels are hard.
Dry cobs well before storage.

soil: Deep black or well-drained loamy soil
tips: Time sowing so that boll formation does not coincide with heavy rain.
Use pheromone traps to monitor pink bollworm.
Destroy crop residue after the last picking.

stages.name: Establishment
tasks: Maintain a uniform plant stand; gap-fill within a week of sowing.
Do the first weeding at 20-25 days.
Thin to one healthy plant per hill.

stages.name: Square formation
tasks: Scout for sucking pests: aphids, whitefly and jassids.
Top-dress fertiliser as per soil test.
Put up yellow sticky traps.

stages.name: Flowering and boll formation
tasks: Irrigate at flowering and boll formation; avoid water stress.
Install pheromone traps for pink bollworm and monitor weekly.
Do not spray in the heat of the day or when rain is expected.

stages.name: Boll opening and picking
tasks: Pick fully opened bolls in dry weather and keep the cotton clean and dry.
Pick in 2-3 rounds.
Destroy crop residue after final picking to break the pink bollworm cycle.

soil: Light, loose, well-drained sandy loam or red soil
tips: Loose soil helps pegs enter the ground and pods develop.
Gypsum at flowering helps pod filling in many soils; follow local advice.
Dry pods well to avoid aflatoxin contamination.

stages.name: Emergence
tasks: Treat seed before sowing and sow in loose, well-drained soil.
Gap-fill within 10 days.
Do the first weeding at 15-20 days.

stages.name: Flowering
tasks: Irrigate at flowering if the soil is dry.
Apply gypsum at flowering as per local recommendation.
Scout for leaf spot and leaf-eating caterpillars.

stages.name: Pegging and pod development
tasks: Do not disturb the soil once pegs enter it.
Keep soil moisture even and avoid waterlogging.
Scout for leaf spot and rust.

stages.name: Maturity
tasks: Stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvest.
Check maturity: the inside of the shell darkens and kernels are well filled.
Dry pods thoroughly before storage.

season: Year-round with protection; best in cool season
tips: Use staking to keep fruit off the soil.
Even moisture prevents fruit cracking and blossom end rot.
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops to reduce soil-borne disease.

stages.name: Nursery
tasks: Raise seedlings in a raised bed or protray with treated seed.
Protect seedlings from heavy rain and sucking pests.
Harden seedlings by reducing water a few days before transplanting.

stages.name: Establishment after transplanting
tasks: Transplant in the evening and irrigate lightly.
Gap-fill within a week.
Put up stakes and yellow sticky traps.

stages.name: Flowering and fruit set
tasks: Stake and tie plants; remove lower leaves touching the soil.
Irrigate regularly; avoid big swings in moisture.
Scout for early blight, leaf curl virus and fruit borer.

stages.name: Harvest
tasks: Harvest at the colour-break stage if transporting far; use clean crates.
Remove and destroy diseased plants.
Continue scouting for fruit borer.

soil: Well-drained loam or black soil; avoid waterlogging
tips: Chilli is sensitive to waterlogging; keep good drainage.
Leaf curl is often caused by thrips and mites; scout early.
Dry red chilli on clean sheets or yards, not on bare soil.

stages.name: Nursery
tasks: Treat seed and raise seedlings in a raised bed.
Protect the nursery from heavy rain and sucking pests.
Transplant healthy seedlings at 30-35 days.

stages.name: Vegetative growth
tasks: Transplant in the evening and irrigate lightly.
Weed at 20-25 days after transplanting.
Scout for thrips and mites (upward curling leaves).

stages.name: Flowering and fruiting
tasks: Irrigate regularly; avoid water stress at flowering.
Scout for leaf curl, fruit rot and fruit borer.
Do not spray when rain is expected.

stages.name: Harvest
tasks: Pick fully ripe fruits in several rounds.
Dry red chilli on clean sheets or yards.
Remove and destroy diseased plants.

soil: Deep, well-drained loam or clay loam
tips: Use healthy, disease-free setts and treat them before planting.
Remove and destroy plants showing red rot signs.
Trash mulching saves water and improves soil.

stages.name: Germination
tasks: Use healthy, disease-free setts and treat them before planting.
Keep the soil moist for good germination.
Gap-fill with sprouted setts within 30-45 days.

stages.name: Tillering
tasks: Weed and earth up; apply nitrogen in splits as per recommendation.
Irrigate regularly.
Scout for early shoot borer (dead hearts).

stages.name: Grand growth
tasks: Irrigate every 7-10 days in summer depending on soil.
Prop or tie canes to prevent lodging.
Remove plants showing red rot symptoms and keep the field clean.

stages.name: Maturity and ripening
tasks: Stop irrigation about 3-4 weeks before harvest to help sugar build-up.
Harvest at the maturity advised by the mill.
Cut close to the ground and deliver promptly.

tips: Use disease-free tissue culture plants.
Keep drainage good; waterlogging encourages wilt.
Prop plants against wind when bunches develop.

stages.name: Establishment
tasks: Plant disease-free tissue culture plants in well-drained pits.
Irrigate regularly; avoid waterlogging.
Mulch to retain moisture.

stages.name: Vegetative growth
tasks: Apply manure and fertiliser in splits as per recommendation.
Remove excess suckers and keep one healthy follower.
Remove and destroy plants with bunchy top symptoms.

stages.name: Flowering and bunch development
tasks: Prop plants with bamboo poles against wind.
Cover bunches if practised and remove the male bud after the last hand.
Irrigate regularly.

stages.name: Harvest
tasks: Harvest when fingers are plump and the angular edges round off.
Handle bunches gently to avoid bruising.
Cut down the harvested plant and keep one healthy follower.

tips: Ragi is hardy and suits low-rainfall areas.
Blast disease is the main risk in humid weather.
Dry earheads fully before threshing and storage.

stages.name: Establishment
tasks: Sow seed or transplant 20-25 day old seedlings into a well-prepared bed.
Thin and gap-fill within 10-15 days.
Do the first weeding around 20 days.

stages.name: Tillering
tasks: Top-dress nitrogen as per recommendation.
Do the second weeding at 35-40 days.
Scout for blast on leaves.

stages.name: Flowering
tasks: Irrigate if dry at flowering.
Scout for finger and neck blast.
Keep the field weed-free.

stages.name: Grain filling and maturity
tasks: Harvest when earheads turn brown and grains are hard.
Dry earheads in the sun before threshing.
Store grain only when fully dry.
